request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an **Export claims (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to the people export. All 4 tests in the spec pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

The change is all front end, in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`. No server or stored-data changes were needed, because the claim rows already have everything the file needs.

- **Contents:** the header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim. People are in list order, retired people included. Each person's claims come oldest first, the reverse of the newest-first order on screen.
- **Figures match the screen:** number, due and period are worked out the same way the claim row works them out. A blank number or period stays blank, and a due of `n/a` is written as `n/a`.
- **Format:** quoting and line endings are the same as the people export (a value is quoted when it holds a comma, quote or line break, and every line ends with a line feed). To share that, I moved the people export's download code into a small helper that both buttons use.
- **Layout:** both buttons now sit inside the existing `data-testid="export"` section.

The file includes every claim, deleted ones too, because the claims list on screen shows them all.
